text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: The patient's history of a chronic, pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities without a clear external trigger (medications, bites, or new exposures) and without complete resolution is most consistent with a dermatological condition such as lichen planus, contact dermatitis with an unidentified allergen, or possibly a manifestation of an underlying systemic disease like hepatitis C. To narrow the differential, I would request a skin biopsy of the affected area and a panel of serological tests including liver function tests (LFTs), hepatitis serology, and a complete blood count (CBC).
